question: The determinant $\begin{vmatrix}x&1&0\\0&x&1\\1&0&x\end{vmatrix}$ has the value $9$. Determine the real value of $x$ and verify the result.
explanation:
Expansion along the first row
Expanding the determinant gives $$x\begin{vmatrix}x&1\\0&x\end{vmatrix}-1\begin{vmatrix}0&1\\1&x\end{vmatrix}$$
Evaluation of the smaller determinants
Therefore, the value is $$x(x^2)-[0-(1)(1)]=x^3+1$$
Application of the given condition
Since the determinant equals $9$, $$x^3+1=9$$ Thus, $$x^3=8$$ and hence $$x=2$$
Verification
Substituting $x=2$, the determinant value is $$2^3+1=8+1=9$$
Therefore, the required real value is $x=2$.
